Today we discuss the idea of capital. Now, you may have learned in economics class that capital means money or wealth. What I want to argue to you today is that capital is really a mechanism to extract energy from you. In a universe where consciousness is the universe, what energy ultimately is attention and focus. So, it's not enough for you to work at something; you also have to concentrate on it in order for capital to extract energy from you.

The most basic example is you have a landlord class trying to extract energy from the peasant class. Traditionally, we would have assumed energy as maybe grain. But the problem with this is you're not really extracting much energy from a peasant because it's not that hard to grow grain. Also, grain can be stored. So, in other words, as a landlord, your priority is not just to extract rent but to get the peasant to focus entirely on the task at hand.

The first mechanism is transitioning from slavery to freedom. If you really want to extract value and energy, it's better to give peasants the illusion of freedom rather than enslave them. Give peasants the belief that they control their lives. Another word for freedom is equity. Think of a company where I'm going to give you some equity, and then you work harder because you think you can make more money.

The second trick is making capital more abstract. So, let's use an example: initially, grain was capital. The problem with grain is that you only need so much. As a peasant, you only want to work as much as necessary to grow grain to feed your family and maybe save a little bit. But then we transitioned to gold. People are more greedy, but the problem with gold is there's only a finite amount, and it's hard to locate. Now, what we've done is transitioned to the idea of money. The great innovation of the past 100 years is convincing people that money is God. Money is both nothing and everything, so you can spend your entire life dedicated to achieving it.

The third mechanism of anxiety is creating debt. I'll lend you a million dollars today and you enjoy it, but then you have to spend the rest of your time paying it back. The problem with this is that there's interest, so you can never really pay it back, which causes anxiety. This idea of debt allows me to extract much more value from you than if you were not in debt.

The second tool is the idea of inequality and poverty where a certain class of people are poor and will always be poor. This incentivizes and encourages the middle class to work even harder. The third mechanism of anxiety is wealth destruction, such as war or depression. When the economy collapses and all your wealth vanishes, it forces peasants to work harder because if they store up grain, they wouldn't have to work anymore. As a landlord, you go burn down their grainery. War is not just a mechanism to expand capitalism but also a way to make people more anxious by destroying their wealth.
